subject: Technical acceptance criteria and rollout schedule
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@mercuryfinancial.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercuryfinancial.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical acceptance criteria and rollout schedule

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Per your RFP request we'd like to confirm the technical acceptance criteria (TAC) and propose a constrained rollout schedule that aligns with Mercury Financial's risk gates. Attached are: 1) Redwood_Technical-Acceptance-Criteria.xlsx (detailed pass/fail checks and metrics), 2) Redwood_Onboarding_SOW.pdf (milestones & responsibilities), and 3) network-requirements-diagram.png.

High-level proposal (please review and flag anything that needs revision):
- Phase 0: Pre-onboarding (security review, VPN/KMS handshake, test keys) — 2 weeks
- Phase 1: Staging integration (API integration, mapping, instrumentation) — 2 weeks
- Phase 2: Canary A (limited production traffic, 0.5% of live sessions or ~500 p95 requests/day) — 1 week
- Phase 3: Canary B (broader sampling, 2% or ~2,000 p95 requests/day) — 1 week
- Phase 4: Gradual ramp to steady-state (rolling percentage increases; automated rollback if regressions) — 2 weeks

Key TAC items (summary) — see sheet for thresholds:
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency under 120ms for canonical prompts (per model profile)
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx or malformed responses during canary windows
- Quality: Automated eval pass rate >= 92% on pre-defined prompt set
- Observability: Tracing + per-token cost and token-level breakdowns enabled; alerts configured
- Security: TLS mutual auth for private connector and KMS-encrypted logs for PII-bearing requests

Open questions for Mercury (Aisha/Tom):
1) Do you want canaries executed by customer traffic split (recommended) or by synthetic generators?
2) Any additional telemetry or SLOs to bake in (security audit frequency, retention windows)?
3) Are there specific maintenance blackout windows we should avoid for canary runs?

Next steps: if you confirm the TAC in the attached xlsx, we'll produce an updated SOW with fixed dates and a canary runbook. We can start Phase 0 as early as Aug 24 if approvals are in place.

Thanks,

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: Redwood_Technical-Acceptance-Criteria.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: Redwood_Onboarding_SOW.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: network-requirements-diagram.png (png)]

From: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@mercuryfinancial.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercuryfinancial.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical acceptance criteria and rollout schedule

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the attachments. A few clarifying points from Mercury before we sign off: 

- Data residency: we need confirmation that cached KV data for sessions initiated from our tenancy remains in-region (us-east-1). Is there an explicit guarantee in Phase 1/2?
- Canary size: could we reduce Canary A to 250 sessions (we want to be conservative for the first live injection)?
- Monitoring: we require a rolling 24h window of request-level replayability (traces available for at least 7 days) for the canary period.
- Compliance handoff: we need Neha to confirm logs and audit exports satisfy our internal SOC/PCI checklist. Can Neha join the technical kick?

Also — is there a way to have a minimal automated rollback at 0.25% error spike to avoid human-in-the-loop delays?

If you can answer these, we can get legal to run the SOW this week.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Platform Integrations
Mercury Financial

To: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@mercuryfinancial.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@mercuryfinancial.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical acceptance criteria and rollout schedule

Hi Aisha — appreciate the quick review. Answers inline below and proposed adjustments: 

- Data residency: Yes — Redwood will pin KV and prefix caches to the Mercury tenancy in us-east-1 for the duration of the canary and steady-state unless otherwise requested. We'll include a clause in the SOW and the network diagram to show in-region routing. (Neha will confirm KMS key scoping.)

- Canary size: We can reduce Canary A to 250 sessions (your suggestion). To preserve signal we'll extend Canary A to 10 days instead of 1 week at that size so we maintain statistical confidence.

- Monitoring: We will enable request-level tracing with a 7-day retention window for full traces and 90-day aggregated metrics. For the canary window we'll keep full traces accessible to Mercury engineering and provide a replay tool for any failed requests.

- Automated rollback: We support a programmable rollback threshold. Proposal: automatic rollback trigger at a sustained 0.25% increase in 5xx or a 15% degradation in quality evals over a rolling 30-minute window. Ops will receive immediate alerts and an automated rollback will execute if thresholds are met.

Action items we will take this week:
- Neha: prepare a short compliance checklist showing log exports and KMS scoping for Mercury (will attach by Thu EOD).
- Rishi: draft the adjustable canary runbook with automated rollback hooks and alert playbook (target Fri).
- Karthik: update the TAC xlsx and SOW dates for Phase 0 start Aug 24 and updated canary length.

If this looks good I suggest we confirm the SOW with legal and schedule an internal kickoff next Tuesday (Aug 24) for Phase 0.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: proposed-canary-runbook-template.md (md)]

Laura / Karthik —

This looks good to us. A few quick confirmations:
- We accept the reduced Canary A (250 sessions) with the 10-day window.
- Automated rollback thresholds accepted (0.25% sustained error spike or 15% quality drop).
- Please ensure the SOW includes an explicit in-region caching guarantee and the Neha compliance checklist.

I've looped in legal to start SOW review and will circulate a DocuSign link once they approve. Looking forward to kickoff on Aug 24.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
VP, Platform Engineering | Mercury Financial
